steps.text: Mix rhubarb, apples, sugar, water, and cinnamon together in a large saucepan; bring to a boil. Cook over medium heat until fruit is soft, about 20 minutes. Stir in pectin; boil for 5 minutes.

Ladle jam into hot, sterilized jars, filling to within 1/4 inch of the top. Run a clean knife or thin spatula around the insides of the jars to remove any air bubbles. Wipe rims with a moist paper towel to remove any residue. Top with lids and screw rings on tightly.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with water. Bring to a boil and lower jars 2 inches apart into the boiling water using a holder. Pour in more boiling water to cover jars by at least 1 inch. Bring to a rolling boil, cover, and process for at least 10 minutes.

Remove the jars from the stockpot and let rest, several inches apart, for 12 to 24 hours. Press the center of each lid with a finger to ensure the lid does not move up or down. Remove the rings for storage and store in a cool, dark area. Refrigerate jam after opening.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Apple Rhubarb Jam
raw_recipe.description: This easy apple rhubarb jam recipe combines tart and tangy rhubarb and crunchy, bright apples with warm cinnamon for an unexpectedly delicious jam.

review.reviewBody: Love it! Tastes amazing! But, just as a side note, if you're a beginner at canning, apples don't set the same way strawberry or other jams set. It won't be solid, even after the cans seal themselves. Apples have too much acid to set solidly. I learned that from my sister-in-law after I questioned her about the texture of this jam. Thanks for such a great recipe!

I used 4 big cups of rhubarb and the remaining 2 cups a mix of apples and strawberries, and it was delicious. I kept the sugar to 1.5 cups and used the full tablespoon of cinnamon. Such a wonderful jam. I've been caught eating it with a spoon! Far healthier than the strawberry freezer jam I made last (4 cups of sugar to 2 cups of berries!). Also, I don't can, so I let it set up for a day and put it in the freezer. Seems to be working wonderfully!

DELICIOUS! But not as expected. Very apple-y!! Also had to run it through a food mill at the end, as the apples did not entirely cook down enough. There were some awkwardly large chunks I wanted to squish in there.
I would go as far as 4c. rhubarb - 2c. apples or even 5 to 1 for a stronger rhubarb flavor! 
Rather sweet; even with granny smith apples to go with the rhubarb. Tastes like an apple pie jam, really. Will take it into account for next time!
(Also: after waiting the full 20 minutes hoping the apples would finish cooking down, it had cooked to about half the expected amount! I have three sadly empty half-pint jars left, lonely on the counter. Will need to find something else to fill them with. :D )

Very quick and easy recipe. I did reduce the sugar to 1.5 cups and used half Splenda and half sugar. Jam still set very well and was still sweet enough for us. Also did not process. Really enjoying the jam. Next summer I will make a double or triple batch!

I’m sure the recipe is delicious as written but I must confess I tweaked it a bit. Increased the rhubarb to 4 cups as suggested. Also used 1 c. white sugar and 1 c. brown sugar. I don’t like using pectin because to me it adds additional sweetness so I used 1/4 c. lemon juice concentrate as the thickener. Added approximately 1/4 tsp (or maybe less) allspice. It’s delicious! Planning on serving this with pan seared pork chops tonight.

I agree that the apples will set differently from strawberries, as someone mentioned, but it is the opposite of what was said!

Apples are the source of pectin in the packages you buy, and higher in pectin than any other fruit!!! 

So if you use apples, and boil it longer, no pectin is required. Strawberries are one of the few fruits that do not contain much pectin, so for instance, my mum would always put apples in her strawberry jam so no pectin was required. 

If you use strawberries instead, you may need to boil longer and will need the pectin, because rhubarb is low in it too.

I am making a jam similar to this later, but sorry, I am using wild apples (with skins on), no pectin, and much less (unrefined) sugar. We'll see how it goes : ) I am adding the apples to the rhubarb so that pectin isn't required (otherwise I would make pure rhubarb jam). 

So, I haven't made it and won't make it the same, but gave a five star as folks seem to like it : )

I followed suggestions by others and changed the ratio to 4 cups rhubarb, 2 cups apple. I also reduced the sugar to 1.5 cups and kept the cinnamon a 1 Tbsp. It's still setting but tasting it while it cooked it is delicious. Just the right amount of tart/sweet. The cinnamon does change the color of the jam to brown.
excellent recipe. I used five cups frozen Rhubarb and 5 cups frozen strawberries and three packages pectin and it was delicious and it set up nicely

This was a very easy and flavorful recipe!! I used strawberries instead of apples. I also used my food processor to chop the fruit (I don't like big pieces). I simmered the fruit with only 1 1/2 cups of sugar for about 1 hour instead of 20 minutes. The end result turned out great. I will definitely make this recipe again!

This has become my favourite jam. I made it as the recipe but it was just a bit too much cinnamon for me, although very good. I increased it to 6 cups of rhubarb and five Granny Smith apples leaving everything else the same except reduced the cinnamon to 1.5 tsp and it is just as delicious. What I love ve about this recipe is how little sugar it takes. My next experiment was with sour cherries, I used 6 cups rhubarb, 5 cups sour cherry, everything else the same. Very tart, if you like tart this is very delicious. I like tart! Today I am trying blueberry rhubarb with 5 cups blueberries. Will let me ou know how this turns out.

Pretty good. I used 5 cups rhubarb and 3 cups apples. Only 1/2 cup water. Used 1 1/4 cups brown sugar and 1/2 cup white. I used 1 tbsp of cinnamon but would cut that back next time. I also added 1 tsp of vanilla. It still tastes mostly like apple cinnamon. I didn't use the pectin. Made 4 cups total. Will try again.
This turned out amazing! Love this recipe!
I used 4 cups rhubarb and 2 cups apples, 1 teaspoon lemon juice, cinnamon and liquid pectin. Thickened nicely and tastes amazing. I also added a little food colouring.
I followed this to a T and only got 2 half pint jars of brown Jam. Picture shows red jam and makes 6 cups. Am I missing something?
I loved the recipe. I used dry pectin. I was wondering if you could use liquid pectin instead of dry.
I loved it as is!

Wow!! The reviews are spot on. I did Take the advice of some and chose 4 cups of rhubarb and 2 cups of red apples and it tastes like apple pie but with some tartness. My 2nd time canning and this recipe was soooooo easy and fast!!!
Can I leave out the rhubarb? I am not a fan..... also am asking before I make 'em. :)

Excellent recipe, My mom had planted Apple tree and Rhubarb in the garden.
Used both the fruits fresh and made this jam, turned out really good.
Called it:
" Amma's Rhubarb & Apple "
It turned out great haven’t tasted it yet but will soon and instead of using pectin I used a half a pack of strawberry jello to make it strawberry apple rhubarb jam
